meta.name: Score Sheet
meta.notes: Ink-on-ivory score; --c-primary only lights the Play button, playhead, fermata marks and active notes; --c-accent tints expression marks (tags) and sale strikes, both ink-mixed for contrast.

issues: Creativity 8, typography 8, layout 6, polish 4, brand robustness 7, mobile 4, generic-ness 8 (not generic): the concept is strong but its execution falls apart on the page

Reveal-on-scroll relied only on IntersectionObserver. In full-page renders, the bottom third of the homepage (variations, story, stats, quote, gallery, finale) was an empty ivory void. On mobile, the whole product score was blank too
The catalog finale/footer area rendered empty. Its last row of product cards showed blank white images because they were lazy-loaded
Product packshots were cropped with object-fit:cover in a 4:3 box. Brinks coffee bags lost their tops and labels, and drum hardware was clipped
The detail card also cropped the product with cover
The fixed 'Demo redesign' badge sat bottom-left on top of the hero's fermata CTA
The hero's Play trigger, the signature interaction, was a tiny 32px dot that read as an afterthought
Too much dead air between the hero and Movement I (about 250px of empty staff paper)
fixed: Added a failsafe for reveals on both pages: everything resolves 1.8s after load and on beforeprint, so no movement can stay blank. Scroll-driven entrances still play for real users
Product images are now eagerly decoded (async), with no lazy loading, so every note on the stave has its picture
Packshots use object-fit:contain with breathing room on white, multiplied onto the card. Coffee bags and drum hardware now show in full
The detail card image uses contain with padding, giving a clean specimen-style product view
Moved the demo badge bottom-right so it no longer covers the hero CTA
Made the hero Play bigger: a 44px primary disc with an offset ring, so the playhead performance is clearly the hero's second voice
Tightened the gap between the hero and Movement I so the score flows straight from the title page into the first movement
